SCI.independent_truth_basis: Before author content, the actual two figures established a near-horizontal receiving crossbar but no wave/polarization direction. In an explicit ideal electric-dipole model, voltage depends on h_eff dot E, not proof that E is entirely along the rod. In the stated plane-wave model B=(khat cross E)/v. With x along the assumed horizontal rod and z vertical: khat=y, E=x gives B parallel -z; khat=(y+z)/sqrt(2), E=x gives B parallel (y-z), not vertical despite matching; khat=y, E=(x+z)/sqrt(2) gives B parallel (x-z), not vertical despite nonzero axial reception and horizontal propagation. Thus vertical oscillation needs matching and horizontal propagation, not antenna appearance alone.
